properties.statement: `req:thin-install` IS SATISFIED FOR NEW INSTALLS AND NOT FOR OLD ONES, AND THE REQUIREMENT'S OWN AUTHOR HIT THE GAP FOURTEEN DAYS AFTER RAISING IT. Alex asked for this on 2026-07-25 — quoted verbatim inside the requirement: 'you wouldn't need to change anything in your repo again and updates would be confined to the reflow package.' It was accepted. `cap:skills-served` then delivered the forward half: skills come from the binary, the installer copies nothing, and an upgrade leaves a project byte-identical (ver:served-skills, 23 cases in tools/test_init.py). WHAT NOBODY BUILT IS THE ROUTE OUT FOR A PROJECT INSTALLED BEFORE THAT. On 2026-08-08 Alex's project was running binary 0.24.0 against `.reflow2/kit-version.json` 0.11.0 — thirteen versions of frozen kit, exactly the state the requirement's statement describes ('it otherwise freezes at install time while reflow2 keeps moving'). Getting out took EIGHT MANUAL STEPS derived by his agent from first principles: export the design, untrack `.reflow2/`, delete committed skill copies, untrack the MCP configs, replace a long AGENTS.md with the pointer, update .gitignore, rewrite the MCP configs, add a committed export. THE MEASURE OF THE PROBLEM IS THAT TWO AGENTS DERIVED IT INDEPENDENTLY ON THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREED. His agent produced eight steps; I produced seven; they overlap on six. HIS INCLUDED A REGRESSION — rewriting `--graph-path` from absolute to RELATIVE, which is the configuration `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` records as having minted an accidental third graph in Anthony's own hxm_program repo, and which that node calls the severe one of six because it 'produced a WRONG ARTEFACT in the user's repository, silently'. MINE GOT THE STAMP FILENAME WRONG on first pass (`.install-stamp` for `kit-version.json`) and I shipped it to the user flagged as unverified. NEITHER OF US WAS CARELESS; the knowledge is simply scattered across the installer source, three accepted decisions and two verifications, and is re-derived per session. THAT IS THE EXACT FAILURE reflow2's own AGENTS.md names as its reason to exist — 'a stateless agent re-derives the design every session and decides silently over a scope bigger than its memory' — here applied to the MIGRATION rather than the design. WHAT IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE AND CURRENTLY IS NOT, every item drawn from a real miss today: is anything under `.reflow2/` tracked by git (the installer has this check and a one-line fault skips it — fact:defect-installer-cannot-warn-that-the-graph-dir-is-already-tracked); are the MCP configs tracked, carrying absolute paths that are meaningless elsewhere; does `kit-version.json` match the installed kit; do local skill copies exist and differ from the served ones, since a local copy SHADOWS the served one silently; is `--graph-path` absolute; is a committed export present and current against the live graph. SIX CHECKS, ALL DECIDABLE, NONE REQUIRING JUDGEMENT. NOTE WHERE IT CANNOT LIVE: not the MCP surface. `dec:agent-navigates-content` keeps reflow2 out of file IO, and every check above reads the filesystem or shells to git. The kit already ships tools that do exactly this — `reflow2_init.py --check`, `check_kit_manifest.py`, `reflow2_check.py` — so the home is there and the machinery is half-built.
